articles.headline: Wildlife Sanctuary Reports Decline in Illegal Poaching Incidents
articles.summary: A prominent wildlife sanctuary has reported a significant decline in illegal poaching incidents, attributed to intensified patrolling and community engagement. This success bodes well for conservation efforts and the protection of endangered species in the region.

articles.headline: Local Theatres Stage Revival of Classic Plays
articles.summary: Local theatre groups are staging a successful revival of classic plays, attracting a new generation of audiences. These productions aim to celebrate theatrical heritage and keep traditional performing arts alive in contemporary settings. Cultural enthusiasts rejoice.

articles.headline: Government Initiatives Promote Scientific Research and Innovation
articles.summary: Government initiatives are actively promoting scientific research and innovation across various fields. Funding for R&D projects, establishment of research centers, and international collaborations are key components aimed at fostering a culture of scientific inquiry and progress.

articles.headline: New Skill Development Centers Open Across States
articles.summary: New skill development centers have been inaugurated across several states, offering vocational training in high-demand industries. These centers aim to enhance employability, empower youth, and meet the growing workforce requirements of a rapidly evolving economy.

articles.headline: Tourism Sector Leverages Digital Marketing for Global Reach
articles.summary: The tourism sector is increasingly leveraging digital marketing strategies to reach a global audience. Online campaigns, social media engagement, and virtual tours are being used to showcase destinations and attract international visitors. This strategy boosts visibility.

articles.headline: Efforts Underway to Clean Major Rivers and Water Bodies
articles.summary: Significant efforts are underway to clean and rejuvenate major rivers and water bodies nationwide. Projects involve community participation, advanced purification technologies, and stricter regulation of industrial discharge to restore ecological balance and water quality.

articles.headline: Regional Cuisine Gains Popularity Through Food Festivals
articles.summary: Regional cuisines are gaining widespread popularity through various food festivals and culinary events. These gatherings celebrate diverse flavors, traditional recipes, and local produce, promoting culinary heritage and boosting food tourism across the country.

articles.headline: Government Simplifies Business Registration Process
articles.summary: The government has simplified the business registration process, aiming to reduce bureaucratic hurdles and encourage entrepreneurship. New online portals and single-window clearances are facilitating easier setup for new businesses, boosting ease of doing business rankings.

articles.headline: Advancements in Remote Sensing Technology Aid Urban Planning
articles.summary: Recent advancements in remote sensing technology are significantly aiding urban planning and development. Satellite imagery and geospatial data provide crucial insights for infrastructure projects, disaster management, and sustainable city growth. This technology improves efficiency.

articles.headline: EPFO enables smooth fund flow for sunset years with systematic withdrawal plan
articles.summary: EPFO approved a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retirees, allowing periodic withdrawals over 20 years, with remaining balances earning interest. The partial withdrawal limit for existing members was raised to 90%. This offers greater flexibility in managing retirement savings and aims to attract gig and unorganized workers for direct contributions.

articles.headline: Tata Sons board reviews Air India’s performance
articles.summary: Tata Sons board members, including Chairman N Chandrasekaran and Noel Tata, reviewed loss-making Air India's performance at its Gurugram headquarters. The review precedes Air India's board meeting on Friday, which will discuss integrating operations, cost rationalization, and fleet upgrades amid a ~22,000 crore loss in FY26.

articles.headline: Airtel is India’s most valuable brand: BrandZ report
articles.summary: Airtel displaced HDFC Bank to become India’s most valuable brand in Kantar's BrandZ 2026 report, valued at $43.2 billion. This is the first time a telecom provider has claimed the top spot since 2014. The total value of the top 100 Indian brands declined 12% year-on-year to $460.3 billion.

articles.headline: Hindu share in world population to ease to 14% by 2070
articles.summary: The Pew Research Center projects India's Muslim population share to increase from 15.4% to 19.6% by 2070, while the Hindu share will marginally decline from 79.4% to 75.8%. Globally, Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians by 2035 due to higher fertility rates. Many countries will see a proliferation of 'nones'.

articles.headline: Cyient Semiconductors secures $10 million equity investment from GlobalFoundries
articles.summary: Hyderabad-based Cyient Semiconductors secured a $10 million strategic equity investment from GlobalFoundries at a $490 million pre-money valuation. The funds will expand Cyient's custom ASIC capabilities and silicon development, strengthening its R&D roadmap in custom power semiconductors, validation, and testing infrastructure in India.

articles.headline: Japan to use Indian test firing ranges from next year
articles.summary: Japan's military will use firing ranges in India, including Chandipur, for live-fire training, starting next year with surface-to-ship missile exercises. This follows the India-Japan 2+2 meeting, deepening bilateral military cooperation and strengthening resilience amid global challenges. Both nations reiterated concerns over economic coercion.

articles.headline: Anthropic raises $81 bn, set to secure $1.8 trn valuation in Nasdaq debut
articles.summary: AI company Anthropic is set to secure a $1.8 trillion valuation on its Nasdaq debut, raising $81.3 billion. Its stock is projected to open 20% higher than its $83 IPO price, defying recent market skepticism over AI investment costs and valuation concerns. This follows strong earnings from Nvidia.

articles.headline: Putin, Xi, Trump discuss nuclear arms, Ukraine war, Taiwan, trade
articles.summary: In a trilateral meeting, Presidents Putin, Xi, and Trump agreed nuclear war must never be fought, reaffirmed arms control, and discussed regional conflicts. Xi urged Trump to address Taiwan issues correctly to avoid US-China setbacks. Tensions over trade and technology, including Nvidia chip diversions to China, remained.

articles.headline: Incentives needed to channel savings into assets: DIPAM secy
articles.summary: DIPAM Secretary Arunish Chawla urged policy, regulatory, and tax incentives to channel household savings into financial assets, formalizing the financial system to meet investment needs. He noted increased household participation in markets, with demat accounts growing sixfold since 2019 and mutual fund AUM rising from ~15 trillion to ~84 trillion.

articles.headline: Fairfax Financial takes control of IIFL Capital
articles.summary: Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings became the controlling shareholder of IIFL Capital, raising its stake to 44.06% through an open offer. The move, following Fairfax's sale of its IIFL Finance stake, is aimed at funding the acquisition of 60% in IDBI Bank from the government and LIC.

articles.headline: Aadhaar card by itself not proof of date of birth: Delhi High Court
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court ruled that an Aadhaar card alone is not sufficient proof of date of birth, clarifying that the Aadhaar Act, 2016 recognizes it only as proof of identity. UIDAI records dates of birth based on documents or self-declaration, not as verified proof.

articles.headline: Sebi, NISM mull learning network for independent directors
articles.summary: Sebi is exploring a Capacity Building Network for independent directors to strengthen boardroom oversight and equip them for challenges like AI, cybersecurity, and data governance. Sebi Chairman Madhabi Puri Buch stated that the network will offer peer learning, case studies, and good governance practices, complementing regulatory initiatives.

articles.headline: HC backs Mauritius co in MF unit sale tax case
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court ruled that gains from selling equity mutual fund units by a Mauritius-based investor cannot be taxed as gains from selling underlying Indian shares under the India-Mauritius tax treaty. This settles a ₹593.48 crore tax dispute and could boost foreign investment via Mauritius.

articles.headline: TN minister chased elephant in Mudumalai, not Karnataka
articles.summary: A video allegedly showing TN minister Vanni Arasu chasing elephants and a tiger sparked controversy. Karnataka forest officials clarified the elephant chase was in Mudumalai (Tamil Nadu), while his Bandipur visit (Karnataka) had no violations. Karnataka's IT minister ordered an inquiry.

articles.headline: Punjab & Haryana HC Stays PCS Selection Amid Irregularity Allegations
articles.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court stayed the Punjab Civil Services recruitment process amid petitions alleging large-scale irregularities. Concerns include multiple roll numbers, altered eligibility criteria, and unsealed question papers.

articles.headline: SC upholds interim bail for Azam Khan in money laundering
articles.summary: The Supreme Court refused to interfere with Allahabad HC's order granting interim bail to Samajwadi Party functionary Azam Khan in a money laundering case. ED's plea was dismissed, with SC clarifying HC's observations were prima facie and wouldn't affect final adjudication.

articles.headline: Kolathur MLA V S Babu, Stalin's defector, dies at 75
articles.summary: Kolathur MLA V S Babu, who defeated former CM M K Stalin in 2026, died at 75 after a prolonged respiratory illness. His death, following 70 days in intensive care, is a loss for TVK, with CM Joseph Vijay and other leaders expressing condolences.

articles.headline: Assam Medical College Withdraws Advisory Asking PGTs to Defer Marriage
articles.summary: Assam Medical College and Hospital withdrew an advisory asking postgraduate trainees (PGTs) in General Medicine to defer marriage until residency completion. The United Doctors Front criticized it as an attempt to put personal lives on hold, highlighting workload issues.

articles.headline: Bank of America signs ₹1,450 cr Hyderabad office lease
articles.summary: Bank of America's captive services arm, BA Continuum India, leased 1 million sq ft of office space at Mindspace Cyberabad in Hyderabad for ₹1,450 crore. This is one of the year's largest office leasing deals, driven by global capability centers' demand.

articles.headline: AI giant Anthropic's IPO soars 30% on Nasdaq debut
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq, with shares spiking over 30% above its $83 IPO price. The offering, valued at $1.5 trillion, is the largest on record, surpassing SpaceX, despite investor fears of an AI bubble and recent turmoil at Nvidia.

articles.headline: IMF chief warns AI market correction 'little bit more' to go
articles.summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva anticipates "perhaps a little bit more" correction in financial markets related to artificial intelligence (AI). This comes amid concerns the AI boom has been overdone and as the US cracks down on high-end chip smuggling to China.

articles.headline: New Zealand Fights Back After India's Early Test Wickets
articles.summary: In the first Test, Jasprit Bumrah made early inroads, reducing New Zealand to 70/5. However, India's supporting bowlers failed to capitalize, allowing Henry Nicholls (113*) and Glenn Phillips (94*) to lead New Zealand's fightback to 243/5 at stumps on Day 1.

articles.headline: Trump, Xi, Putin sign peace pledge amid global conflicts
articles.summary: US, Chinese, and Russian presidents signed a "peace declaration" at a three-way meeting, reaffirming nuclear war should not be fought. No arms-control commitments were made. The declaration mentioned UN reform, energy supply, immunity of state officials, and reducing nuclear risks. It did not mention Ukraine or Iran conflicts.

articles.headline: PM Modi uses GTA VI to showcase India's growth
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI to create a "national scoreboard" on social media, listing India's progress since GTA V (2013). He highlighted economic growth, poverty reduction, and expansion in various sectors.

articles.headline: Trump: US will 'see what happens' in Iran conflict
articles.summary: President Donald Trump said the US would "see what happens" in its conflict with Iran after January 1, without explaining the date's significance. He downplayed threats of a "dirty bomb" but mentioned Iran potentially looking at biological/chemical weapons.

articles.headline: Xi urges US to do 'right thing' on Taiwan for stable ties
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping told US President Donald Trump that the US must "keep doing the right thing" on Taiwan to avoid "great turbulence" in Sino-American relations. Xinhua reported Trump affirmed Washington "does not support 'Taiwan independence'".

articles.headline: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
articles.summary: The UN's highest court, the ICJ, ruled that Myanmar's security forces committed state-sponsored genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority in 2017. This landmark decision, the first time the court held a state responsible for genocide, mandates compensation and safe return for Rohingya refugees.

articles.headline: India, Japan commit to free, open world order
articles.summary: India and Japan pledged to uphold a free and open world order in an "increasingly severe" security environment, deepening defence and technology cooperation during their 2+2 dialogue in Tokyo. They agreed to accelerate coordination for Japan to use India’s firing ranges.

articles.headline: Govt extends BS-VI PUC validity, shortens for BS-IV
articles.summary: The Centre altered PUC certificate validity based on emission standard, age, and vehicle type. BS-VI cars/motorcycles up to 6 years old now get 3 years (from 1); older BS-IV vehicles need checks every 6 months (from 1 year). Experts urged better maintenance.

articles.headline: India, Bangladesh risk Ganga treaty lapse in Dec
articles.summary: India and Bangladesh face the lapse of their three-decade Ganga Water Treaty in early December as formal renewal talks haven't begun. Bangladesh sought discussions on Nov 17. Complex issues and political inaction after Sheikh Hasina's ousting have hindered progress.

articles.headline: Odisha shifts 300,000 as Cyclone Akvan nears
articles.summary: Odisha shifted nearly 300,000 people from vulnerable districts and set up 9,341 shelters as Cyclone Akvan is expected to make landfall near Gopalpur. Andhra Pradesh also advised alertness. This follows the state's improved disaster management since the 1999 Super Cyclone.

articles.headline: SC to decide on Amity University PIL scope in January
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will decide in January whether to continue a nationwide PIL on private university regulation, originating from an individual student's grievance against Amity University, Noida. The court will also consider the inquiry report.

articles.headline: Haryana CM: Domicile quota in private jobs not right approach
articles.summary: Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini reiterated that domicile reservation in private jobs isn't the right approach, but the government offers incentives to companies hiring local youth. He discussed his government's performance, priorities, and views on BJP's ties with SAD.

articles.headline: Two die, six injured in Delhi Kashmere Gate hit-and-run
articles.summary: Two pedestrians died and six were injured after a speeding Toyota Fortuner rammed an auto-rickshaw and pedestrians near Kashmere Gate. The 23-year-old accused driver is absconding, suspected of drunk driving. A case under BNS sections 281 and 105 has been filed.

articles.headline: Anthropic raises record $107.3bn, topping SpaceX IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic raised a record $107.3 billion in an upsized IPO and private placement, becoming the first frontier AI lab to tap public markets. The $81.3 billion base deal topped SpaceX's, with demand nearly seven times the available shares.

articles.headline: Penhold grip in table tennis a dying art
articles.summary: The penhold grip, a technique once dominant in table tennis, is now rare, used by only two of the top 20 male players. France's Felix Lebrun, a Paris Olympics medalist, stands out using this grip. It offers wrist flexibility and fast forehand attacks, but modern balls and shakehand dominance reduced its power.

articles.headline: MP High Court slams state for 'blind' AI use, fake judgment
articles.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court criticized the state government for "callous and irresponsible" drafting, citing a non-existent Supreme Court judgment attributed to "blindly resorting" to AI tools. The court quashed a sub-inspector's dismissal, calling the state's justification unsustainable.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi: India is a 'side player' in global affairs
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi criticized the Union government for making India a "side player" globally. Speaking at University of Chicago, he called for strong ties with US, Russia, China. He also raised concerns about electoral malpractice but ruled out boycotting elections.

articles.headline: Van Gogh's 'Chataigniers en fleurs' sells for record $190.4M
articles.summary: Vincent van Gogh's 1890 painting "Chataigniers en fleurs" sold for a record $190.4 million at Sotheby's, making it the fourth most expensive painting ever sold at auction. The sale resolved claims of Nazi persecution, ensuring compensation for the former Jewish owner's heirs.

articles.headline: Woman plotted IndiGo staffer's murder over affair
articles.summary: A 40-year-old woman was arrested in Maharashtra's Gondia for allegedly hiring three men to murder an IndiGo staffer. She suspected the victim was in a relationship with her husband. The victim died from stab wounds. A ₹13-lakh contract was allegedly fixed for the killing.

articles.headline: Goldy Brar tops Canada's most wanted list
articles.summary: Satinderjeet Singh alias Goldy Brar is now on Canada's most-wanted list, with a reward of up to C$250,000 for information leading to his arrest. He is the first Indian-origin gangster on Canada's and US's top 10 lists, suggesting he may have entered Canada.

articles.headline: COP31 draft drops fossil fuel pledge, cuts finance
articles.summary: The near-final draft of the COP31 decision dropped all references to fossil fuels and a $120 billion adaptation finance target sought by developing countries. Experts criticized it as "regressive." India had opposed a fossil fuel phase-out without financial aid.

articles.headline: Delhi court voids AAP councillor's 2022 election win
articles.summary: A Delhi court set aside the election of AAP councillor Navariya from Pushp Vihar (Ward 166) in the 2022 MCD elections. He was found to have concealed a previous conviction for grievous hurt in his affidavit. BJP candidate Naresh was declared the duly elected councillor.

articles.headline: Chennai stalker dies after assault by target's family
articles.summary: A 28-year-old man who stalked a social media influencer and traveled from Chennai to Delhi to stop her wedding died after being assaulted by her family and a neighbor. Police arrested the woman's father and a tenant for culpable homicide.

articles.headline: Delhi launches 'Ehsaas 2026' mental health policy for students
articles.summary: Delhi government launched "Ehsaas 2026," a mental health policy for students, providing one counselor per 500 students, well-being centers, and specialized services. The policy aims to strengthen emotional support and create a safe learning environment for students.

articles.headline: CM leads cleanliness drive at Munak Canal ghat after Chhath Puja
articles.summary: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta led a cleanliness drive at a Chhath ghat along the Munak Canal in Shalimar Bagh. She emphasized the responsibility to clean surroundings after religious and cultural celebrations.

articles.headline: Yogi Adityanath blames Akhilesh rally for boy's death
articles.summary: UP CM Yogi Adityanath blamed SP chief Akhilesh Yadav's Gorakhpur rally for the death of a BJP member's teen son, who was run over by a payloader showering petals. Adityanath ordered a crackdown on alleged hooliganism and murder charges against the driver and owners.

articles.headline: Bombay HC halts demolition of Dawood's ancestral building
articles.summary: Bombay HC halted the demolition of Haji Ismail Haji Habib Musafrkhana, a 150-year-old prayer hall and Dawood Ibrahim's family's former residence, in Bhendi Bazaar. The court directed status quo, after BMC had already demolished 60-70% of the structure, pending a petition challenging the action.

articles.headline: IAS officer's sons bought 24 villas before corruption FIR
articles.summary: Weeks before an FIR against IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal for favouring a resort, his sons allegedly bought 24 villas there for Rs 2.6 crore (Rs 11 lakh each, against Rs 59 lakh brochure price). The Rajasthan HC declined his plea for interim protection from the ACB probe.

articles.headline: Graca Machel awarded Indira Gandhi Peace Prize
articles.summary: Mozambican humanitarian and rights activist Graca Machel received the 2025 Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development from Sonia Gandhi. Machel was recognized for her life devoted to social justice and human dignity.

articles.headline: 13 convicted in 2012 Kerala activist murder, 2 CPI(M) leaders acquitted
articles.summary: A CBI court in Kerala convicted 13 CPI(M) activists for the 2012 murder of MSF activist Ariyil Abdul Shukoor, sentencing seven to life imprisonment. However, 18 others, including senior CPI(M) leaders P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, were acquitted of conspiracy charges, disappointing the victim's family.

articles.headline: India proposes joint vision for Nepal PM's visit
articles.summary: India proposed a joint vision for economic cooperation, investment, transit, energy, and digital connectivity, to be unveiled during Nepal PM Balen Shah’s visit. Nepal has proposed a $2 billion economic package. The visit aims to reset bilateral ties.

articles.headline: Iran war reshapes global energy markets, IEA warns
articles.summary: The Iran war will leave lasting marks on global energy markets, forcing nations to prioritize security and affordability after record supply disruptions. The IEA's World Energy Outlook suggests oil demand may fall sooner, and gas markets could face a huge imbalance.

articles.headline: Riyadh's tallest building damaged in Houthi attack
articles.summary: Saudi authorities confirmed a Houthi attack damaged a tower in Riyadh’s financial district, hours after an explosion. The civil defence agency reported "material damage but no casualties" to what appeared to be the Public Investment Fund tower, the city’s tallest.

articles.headline: Muhammad Yunus' ancestral home set ablaze
articles.summary: The ancestral home of Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus in Chattogram, Bangladesh, was set on fire late Wednesday. This occurred amidst escalating protests and violence in Bangladesh, where the current interim PM Tarique Rahman has blamed India for unrest.

articles.headline: Rakshitha upstages Tokyo Olympics champion Chen
articles.summary: Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj (world No.47) achieved a stunning 21-18, 24-22 victory over Tokyo Olympics champion Chen Yu Fei (world No.4) at the Hong Kong Open. This win secures her a spot in the quarter-finals, her biggest career achievement at this level.

articles.headline: South Africa records 9-wicket win over Bangladesh
articles.summary: South Africa secured a nine-wicket victory against Bangladesh in the first Test at Johannesburg. Spin bowler Simon Harmer took six wickets and Kagiso Rabada three, dismissing Bangladesh for 168 in their second innings. South Africa easily chased the remaining 12 runs before lunch.

articles.headline: Sri Lanka frustrates Pakistan, avoids innings defeat
articles.summary: Sri Lanka mounted a resilient fightback on Day 3 of the second Test against Pakistan, reaching 309-9. Milan Rathnayaka (60*), Sonal Dinusha (54), and Kusal Mendis (53) defied Pakistan's attack, leading by 82 runs and avoiding an innings defeat.

articles.headline: Ex-players urge sports minister to replace AIFF president
articles.summary: Bhaichung Bhutia leads 15 former national players urging Sports Minister Mandaviya to nominate a proven leader for AIFF, as current president Kalyan Chaubey's term ends. They cite drastically dropped international rankings and poor financial management, risking the future of Indian football.

articles.headline: Bajaj Group invests ₹2,500 cr in healthcare venture
articles.summary: The Bajaj Group is entering corporate healthcare with Nivara, a new venture to establish medical centers, at-home care, and a 500-bed hospital. It plans to invest ₹2,000-2,500 crore, starting with a Pune medical center next week, aiming for six cities in 10 years.

articles.headline: Karnataka HC orders government to identify undocumented forests
articles.summary: Karnataka High Court directed the state government to conduct a comprehensive statewide exercise to identify and map all unnotified or unrecorded forests. The process, including draft inventory and objections, must be completed within nine months, followed by statutory protection.

articles.headline: SC: Commercial courts must vet bank-builder nexus in loan recovery
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that commercial courts must determine the nexus between builders and bank officials before ordering homebuyers to repay loans for incomplete projects. It stressed no coercive action without determining if homebuyers are in default, protecting them from fraudulent schemes.

articles.headline: HC quashes NEET phone notice, protects meritorious student
articles.summary: Karnataka HC quashed NTA's notice to a medical student for allegedly carrying a mobile phone to a cancelled NEET exam, ordering her marks card release. The court stated that merit shouldn't be penalized by "technical rigidity" or unproven malpractice claims.

articles.headline: Sikh owner plans Sonia Gandhi's Italy home museum
articles.summary: Sukhdev Singh Kang, the Sikh owner of Sonia Gandhi's ancestral home in Lusiana, Italy, plans to convert it into a museum. He is preserving the house as it was and seeks to collaborate with the Gandhi family to display personal belongings, honoring her journey.

articles.headline: Ben Shelton close to ATP Finals semifinals
articles.summary: American Ben Shelton defeated Rafael Jodar 7-6 (10/8), 7-5, moving closer to the semifinals of the ATP Finals with his second win in three group-stage matches.

articles.headline: Kannada, Tulu cinema shine at IFFI 2026
articles.summary: Five films from Karnataka, including Kannada and Tulu cinema, are featured at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. This highlights changing perceptions of regional cinema and the need for more diverse storytelling, from folklore-driven blockbusters to documentaries.

articles.headline: Filmmaker urges inclusive storytelling at queer film festival
articles.summary: Filmmaker Roopa Rao advocates for the KASHISH queer film festival to be open to all audiences, not just the community. She emphasizes the need for diverse stories, especially in local languages with subtitles, to challenge stereotypes and ensure authentic portrayals by queer and non-queer filmmakers.

articles.headline: PM slams industry leaders over static wages, employment
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticized industry leaders for lack of progress in manufacturing, failure to increase employment and wages, and exporters sending best items abroad. He urged them to exploit Free Trade Agreement benefits.

articles.headline: Boy’s death sparks row between U.P. CM, SP president
articles.summary: A war of words erupted between UP CM Yogi Adityanath and SP chief Akhilesh Yadav over the death of a 14-year-old boy, allegedly hit by a bulldozer during Mr. Yadav’s rally. An FIR has been lodged.

articles.headline: OPEC share in India’s crude imports dropped in April-Oct.
articles.summary: OPEC's share in India's crude oil imports declined to 27.4% in April-Oct., from 38.5% last year, reflecting a shift towards Eurasian and North American supplies due to West Asia conflict.

articles.headline: Tata Electronics flags supply chain, talent gaps in chip push
articles.summary: Tata Electronics faces challenges in building semiconductor manufacturing in India, including developing local suppliers, transporting specialized equipment, and bridging talent gaps.
